cards.back: Production failures become new golden questions, so the same bug cannot come back silently.
An end-to-end score tells you something got worse; component scores tell you where.
Relevant chunks in the top k ÷ all relevant chunks for that question. 3 of 4 gold chunks in the top 5 gives recall@5 = 0.75.
1 if any gold chunk is in the top k, else 0. Use it when the same fact lives in several chunks and finding one is enough.
MRR 0.5 means the first right chunk is typically at rank 2; 0.33 means rank 3.
Each result earns its relevance grade discounted by log₂(rank + 1), divided by the ideal order. It sees reorders inside the top k that recall can't.
Groundedness checks every claim is supported by the retrieved context, not that it is true. Faithfully repeating stale context scores 1.0 and is still wrong.
Judges prefer longer answers, the first option in a pair and their own model family. Shuffle order, cap length and use a different family.
Fake but realistic tools; score task success from the final state, plus steps, tokens, latency and any forbidden calls.
Common, exact-ID, multi-hop, stale, no-answer, permission and injection cases. Start with 100 to 300 and grow from production.
An offline library that runs the golden set in CI (Ragas, DeepEval, promptfoo) plus a tracing platform that scores production traffic (Langfuse, Phoenix, LangSmith).

quiz.q: Recall@5 is 0.4. Which change can fix the answers?
choices: Improving retrieval: chunking, embeddings or hybrid search
quiz.why: If recall@k is low the model never saw the right text, so no prompt can fix it.

quiz.q: A reranker reorders results inside the top 5. Which metric shows the change?
quiz.why: Recall@k ignores order within the top k; nDCG rewards the best chunks near the top.

quiz.q: A multi-hop question needs two sections. It scores MRR 1.0 but still fails. Why?
choices: MRR only scores the first relevant chunk
quiz.why: Pair MRR with recall@k to see the second, third or fourth relevant chunk.

quiz.q: A candidate improves recall and groundedness but correct refusals drop from 100% to 97%. Ship it?
choices: No; one failed safety rule blocks the release
quiz.why: Safety rules must be perfect, whatever the averages say.

quiz.q: Recall dropped after relabelling. What should you check before trusting it?
choices: Review the misses by hand for unlabelled relevant chunks
quiz.why: Incomplete labels count a correct find as a miss.

quiz.q: A judge passes an answer saying 14 weeks where the source says 12. What fixes this?
choices: Ask for the evidence quote and spot-check numbers with code
Trust it once it is above 0.95
quiz.why: Lenient judges pass paraphrases that change numbers.

quiz.q: Before an LLM judge gates releases, how do you calibrate it?
choices: Label 100 to 200 answers by hand and require at least 85% agreement
Compare it with another tool's faithfulness score
quiz.why: A judge is a measuring instrument; never compare numbers across tools.
